aerosol_cans.description: Aerosol cans made of steel or aluminum are recyclable once they are completely empty. Do not puncture or crush. Check with local recycling for specific rules on pressurized containers.
aerosol_cans.how_to_recycle: Ensure the can is completely empty. Do not puncture or crush. Place in curbside recycling if accepted.

aluminum_food_cans.description: Aluminum food cans are widely accepted in curbside recycling programs. Rinse them to remove food residue before placing in the recycling bin.
aluminum_food_cans.how_to_recycle: Rinse out food residue. Place in curbside recycling.

aluminum_soda_cans.description: Rinse soda cans to remove sugary residues. Aluminum is highly recyclable and can be endlessly reused.
aluminum_soda_cans.how_to_recycle: Rinse to remove any sugary residue. Crush gently to save space and place in curbside recycling.

cardboard_boxes.description: Flatten cardboard boxes to save space. Ensure they are clean and dry without food contamination.
cardboard_boxes.how_to_recycle: Flatten the boxes. Remove any tape or labels if possible. Place in dry recycling bin.

cardboard_packaging.description: Remove any plastic or foam inserts before recycling cardboard packaging. Keep it dry and clean.
cardboard_packaging.how_to_recycle: Remove any non-paper inserts (like foam or plastic). Flatten and place in recycling.

clothing.description: Not accepted in curbside recycling. Donate usable clothing or bring to textile recycling centers to avoid landfill.
clothing.how_to_recycle: Donate usable items. For unusable clothing, take to textile recycling centers.

coffee_grounds.description: Coffee grounds are not recyclable but are compostable. They enrich compost with nitrogen and organic matter.
coffee_grounds.how_to_recycle: Collect used grounds and add to compost bin.

disposable_plastic_cutlery.description: These items are made from low-grade plastic and are typically too small to be sorted effectively. Place in trash.
disposable_plastic_cutlery.how_to_recycle: Not recyclable. Dispose of in trash.

eggshells.description: Eggshells should be composted, not recycled. They add calcium to compost and break down easily.
eggshells.how_to_recycle: Add to compost bin to enrich with calcium.

food_waste.description: Food waste is not recyclable but should be composted where facilities exist. Keep food out of recycling bins.
food_waste.how_to_recycle: Collect in a compost bin or use municipal composting services if available.

glass_beverage_bottles.description: Remove caps and rinse bottles before recycling. Avoid mixing broken glass which can damage sorting equipment.
glass_beverage_bottles.how_to_recycle: Remove caps. Rinse and place in glass recycling bin.

glass_cosmetic_containers.description: Clean thoroughly to remove residues. Containers made of glass (not plastic parts) can be recycled.
glass_cosmetic_containers.how_to_recycle: Remove any non-glass parts. Rinse thoroughly and recycle the glass part.

glass_food_jars.description: Rinse food jars and remove lids. Labels can stay on, but avoid jars with mixed materials like metal or plastic coatings.
glass_food_jars.how_to_recycle: Remove lids. Rinse thoroughly. Labels can stay on. Place in glass recycling.

magazines.description: Glossy paper from magazines is accepted in most paper recycling programs. Stack or bundle if required by local rules.
magazines.how_to_recycle: Bundle together if required. Place in paper recycling.

newspaper.description: Newspapers are ideal for recycling. Keep dry and unsoiled by food or grease for proper processing.
newspaper.how_to_recycle: Keep clean and dry. Place in paper recycling bin.

office_paper.description: Includes printer paper, envelopes (without plastic windows), and notepaper. Keep it clean and dry.
office_paper.how_to_recycle: Stack or loosely place in paper recycling. Avoid plastic windowed envelopes.

paper_cups.description: Most paper cups are lined with plastic, making them hard to recycle. Compost if labeled compostable.
paper_cups.how_to_recycle: Dispose of in compost bin if compostable. Otherwise, place in trash.

plastic_cup_lids.description: Small and often made of mixed materials, these are not accepted in most recycling systems. Dispose in trash.

plastic_detergent_bottles.description: Rinse and remove pump tops if applicable. Bottles are usually made of HDPE, a highly recyclable plastic.
plastic_detergent_bottles.how_to_recycle: Rinse. Remove pump tops. Place bottle in plastic recycling bin.

plastic_food_containers.description: Clean containers of any food residue. Containers with recycling numbers #1 or #2 are most widely accepted.
plastic_food_containers.how_to_recycle: Clean out all food residue. Place in plastic recycling bin if marked #1 or #2.

plastic_shopping_bags.description: Do not put in curbside recycling. Return to designated grocery store bins for proper recycling.
plastic_shopping_bags.how_to_recycle: Collect and return to designated store drop-off locations.

plastic_soda_bottles.description: Made from PET plastic, these are widely accepted. Remove caps and rinse before recycling.
plastic_soda_bottles.how_to_recycle: Remove caps. Rinse and place in curbside recycling.

plastic_straws.description: Too small and lightweight for recycling machines. Place in trash to avoid contaminating recycling streams.
plastic_straws.how_to_recycle: Place in trash. Too small for recycling.

plastic_trash_bags.description: Not recyclable. If they contain recyclables, empty the contents into the bin and dispose of the bag in trash.
plastic_trash_bags.how_to_recycle: Empty contents into bin. Dispose bag in trash.

plastic_water_bottles.description: Rinse and flatten if possible. Remove caps, which are often made from a different type of plastic.
plastic_water_bottles.how_to_recycle: Remove caps. Rinse, flatten if possible, and place in recycling.

shoes.description: Shoes are not curbside recyclable. Donate usable pairs or take to specialized shoe recycling programs.
shoes.how_to_recycle: Donate if wearable. Otherwise, take to specialty shoe recycling programs.

steel_food_cans.description: Rinse to remove food residue. Labels can remain. Steel is fully recyclable and valuable.
steel_food_cans.how_to_recycle: Rinse. Labels may stay on. Place in metal recycling.

styrofoam_cups.description: Styrofoam is not accepted in most recycling programs due to contamination and processing issues. Place in trash.

styrofoam_food_containers.description: Not recyclable due to food contamination and material challenges. Best disposed in trash.
styrofoam_food_containers.how_to_recycle: Dispose in trash. Not recyclable due to contamination.

tea_bags.description: Compost if made of natural fibers (paper or cotton). Plastic mesh bags should go in the trash.
tea_bags.how_to_recycle: Compost if made of paper or cotton. Trash for synthetic bags.
